brief.offer: Video case studies with engineering teams that use your product

facts.claim: Tuple is a remote pair programming app for developers.
facts.excerpt: Tuple is an app for remote pair programming, optimized for everything that developers care about:

facts.claim: Tuple describes itself as the best remote pair programming app on macOS and Windows.
facts.excerpt:
# Tuple

The best remote pair programming app on macOS and Windows

facts.claim: Tuple emphasizes fast, clear screen sharing and good call quality in customer testimonials on its site.
facts.excerpt: It's fast - Call quality is good - It really feels like we are working on the same computer

facts.claim: Tuple has a Slack integration that starts pairing sessions from channels or DMs with a /tuple command.
facts.excerpt: Tuple's integration for Slack adds a `/tuple` command, which will start a pairing session directly from a channel or DMs.

facts.claim: Tuple offers an educational free-forever account if users email support.
facts.excerpt: if you email support@tuple.app and say you want to use Tuple for educational purposes, we'll make you a free-forever account.
facts.source_title: Tuple: Pair Programming Tool for macOS | Hacker News

research.website_note: The tuple.app site and linked profiles describe Tuple as the same company behind the remote pair programming app.

strategy.observation: Tuple is a remote pair programming app for developers, and its site already leans on customer proof around fast, clear screen sharing and good call quality.
strategy.offer_link: Video case studies featuring engineering teams who use Tuple would give marketing a stronger way to demonstrate those core product benefits to technical buyers, rather than only describing them in text.
hypotheses: The marketing team may be looking for new proof assets to support developer-focused demand generation.
Engineering customers may be willing to appear on camera and speak credibly about how Tuple works in practice.
Video testimonials could help Tuple differentiate on quality-of-experience claims like screen sharing and call clarity.
strategy.angle: Tuple already sells around fast screen sharing and call quality, so engineering-team video case studies could turn those claims into proof prospects can watch.
strategy.fit_reason: Tuple serves developer teams, and the product is already positioned with experience-based claims that are well suited to video case studies from real engineering users. That makes the offer a natural marketing asset rather than a forced fit.

draft.subject: Video proof for Tuple
draft.body:
Tuple already sells around fast screen sharing and call quality. If those are core buying points, video case studies with engineering teams would turn them into proof prospects can watch, not just read.

I make short video case studies with engineering teams. The goal is to give marketing a stronger asset for technical buyers without adding much lift on your side.

Are you open to a pilot with one team already using Tuple?
